t.6.113.1: Having beheld Ayodhyā, Rāghava fell to thinking; and having reflected, he then cast his gaze upon the Vānaras.
t.6.113.2: Then wise and radiant Rāma, wishing to do what would please, spoke to his dear Hanumān, the monkey of swift prowess.
t.6.113.3: Go swiftly to Ayodhyā with all haste, O best of monkeys, and find out whether the people in the king's palace are well.
t.6.113.4: Having reached Śṛṅgaverapura, convey my greetings of well-being, in my name, to Guha, lord of the Niṣādas, who dwells in the deep forest.
t.6.113.5: Hearing that I am well, free from illness and rid of fever, Guha will be pleased, he who is my friend, equal to my own self.
t.6.113.6: Guha, the lord of the Niṣādas, being pleased, will tell you the way to Ayodhyā and the news of Bharata.
t.6.113.7: But Bharata must be told by you, in my words, of my welfare; announce to him that I have accomplished my purpose, together with my wife and with Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.113.8: And also the abduction of Vaidehī by the mighty Rāvaṇa, the conversation with Sugrīva, and the slaying of Vālin in battle.
t.6.113.9: The search for Maithilī, and how she was found by you after you had leapt across the imperishable lord of rivers with its vast waters.
t.6.113.10: The approach to the ocean and the sight of the sea, how the bridge was caused to be built, and how Rāvaṇa was slain.
t.6.113.12: Having conquered the hosts of his enemies and won unsurpassed glory, the mighty Rāma, his purpose fulfilled, is coming together with his friends.
t.6.113.11: The granting of boons by Mahendra, Brahmā and Varuṇa, and, through the grace of Mahādeva, my meeting with my father.
t.6.113.14: All the news and all the gestures of Bharata are to be truly discerned, through the color of his face, his glance, and his manner of speaking.
t.6.113.13: Whatever expression Bharata then assumes on hearing this, that should be discerned by you, and also everything in his disposition toward me.
t.6.113.15: For whose mind would not be turned by an ancestral kingdom, handed down from father and grandfather, abounding in all objects of desire and crowded with elephants, horses and chariots?
t.6.113.16: If, through long association with it, the illustrious Bharata should himself come to desire the kingdom, then let that delight of the Raghus rule the whole, entire earth.
t.6.113.17: Having learned his mind and his resolve, O monkey, you should return quickly, before we have gone far.
t.6.113.18: Thus instructed, Hanūmān, the son of Māruta, assumed a human form and went swiftly to Ayodhyā.
t.6.113.20: Having reached Śṛṅgaverapura and approached Guha, the mighty Hanūmān, filled with joy, spoke these words to him in an auspicious voice.
t.6.113.19: Having passed beyond the path of the ancestors and the auspicious abode of the lord of serpents, and having crossed the fearsome confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā,
t.6.113.21: Your friend Rāma, the Kākutstha of true valor, together with Sītā and with Saumitri, has asked after your welfare.
t.6.113.22: Having stayed, at the sage's word, through the fifth night today, Rāghava has been given leave by Bharadvāja, and you will see him this very day.
t.6.113.23: Having spoken thus, the greatly splendid one, his body's hair bristling with delight, leapt up, swift and of mighty speed, without hesitating.
t.6.113.24: He saw Rāmatīrtha, and likewise the river Vālukinī; he saw that Gomatī too, and likewise the dreadful forest of sāla trees.
t.6.113.25: Having travelled a long way in haste, that elephant among monkeys came upon trees in full blossom growing near Nandigrāma.
t.6.113.27: He wore matted locks, his limbs smeared with dirt, and he was emaciated by grief over his brother's misfortune; he lived on fruits and roots, self-restrained, an ascetic who walked the path of righteousness.
t.6.113.26: But at a distance of just a krośa from Ayodhyā he saw Bharata, clad in bark garments and a black antelope skin, wretched and emaciated, living in a hermitage.
t.6.113.29: Placing those two sandals before him, he rules the earth, the protector of the people of the four varṇas from danger on every side.
t.6.113.28: Him, bearing a heavy mass of matted locks piled high, clad in bark garments and deerskin, self-restrained, his spirit purified, and equal in splendor to a brahmarṣi.
t.6.113.31: For those citizens, devoted to dharma, cannot bring themselves to abandon that prince clad in bark garments and black antelope skin.
t.6.113.30: Him, attended by ministers and by pure family priests, and by the chiefs of the army, disciplined men clad in ochre garments.
t.6.113.33: That Kākutstha, for whom you grieve as one dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest, wearing bark garments and matted locks, has asked after your welfare.
t.6.113.32: To him, who knew dharma and was like Dharma itself, like another Devavant, Hanumān, the son of Māruta, spoke these words with joined palms.
t.6.113.35: Having slain Rāvaṇa and regained Maithilī, Rāma, his purpose accomplished, is drawing near together with his mighty friends.
t.6.113.34: I bring you joyful news, O lord: you shall cast off your dreadful grief. In this very moment you are united with your brother Rāma.
t.6.113.36: Lakṣmaṇa of great splendour is well, and so is the illustrious Vaidehī; Sītā is united with Rāma, as Śacī is with the great Indra.
t.6.113.37: Thus addressed by Hanumān, Bharata, the son of Kaikayī, overjoyed, suddenly fell down, and from sheer joy he lost consciousness.
t.6.113.38: Then, after a moment, having risen and recovered himself, Bharata, the descendant of Raghu, spoke these words to Hanūmān, the bearer of pleasing tidings.
t.6.113.39: Embracing the monkey in his excitement, the illustrious Bharata bathed him with large drops of tears, born of joy and full of love.
t.6.113.40: Whether you are a god or a man, you have come here out of compassion; O gentle one, to you, the bearer of pleasing news who speaks what is dear, I give something pleasing in return.
t.6.113.41: A hundred thousand cows, a full hundred villages, and sixteen maidens of virtuous conduct, adorned with earrings, to be your wives.
t.6.113.43: Then, having heard from the foremost of monkeys the news of Rāma's return, which was like a marvel, the king's son was filled with delight and longed to see Rāma, and again, out of joy, he spoke these words.
t.6.113.42: Women of golden complexion, with lovely noses and thighs and faces gentle as the moon, adorned with every ornament and endowed with noble family and birth.
